10 units, each with worked examples, a 10-mark practice set in CBSE question styles, common mistakes and quick recall

How this book matches your board exam. Research check: this book follows the prose chapters and the play in NCERT's First Flight for CBSE Class 10 English Language and Literature (184), 2026–27 session. The English paper is 80 marks in 3 hours, plus 20 marks of internal assessment. Section C (Literature, 40 marks) includes a 5-mark extract from prose or drama, four 3-mark short answers on First Flight (from a choice of five, 40–50 words each), and one 6-mark long answer on First Flight (100–120 words). The two board exams continue: Phase 1 is compulsory, and Phase 2 is optional for improving marks.

About the texts. This book does not reproduce the NCERT texts. It gives our own summaries, character notes and themes, so keep your textbook beside you and read each chapter first. Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set (a 1-mark MCQ, a 3-mark short answer and a 6-mark long answer). The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme. Check the latest syllabus on cbseacademic.nic.in.

Unit 1 of 10: A Letter to God

Key ideas

  • Author: G.L. Fuentes.
  • Summary: Lencho, a farmer, lives in the only house on the crest of a low hill, overlooking his field of ripe corn. He hopes for rain, and it comes — but turns into a violent hailstorm that destroys the crop. Lencho has complete faith in God. He writes a letter to God asking for 100 pesos to resow and survive until the next harvest, and posts it. The postmaster laughs at first, but is moved by Lencho's faith. To keep that faith alive, he collects money from his employees and friends, and gives part of his own salary. He can gather only a little more than half — 70 pesos — and sends it signed "God". Lencho is not surprised to receive money, but is angry that it is less than he asked for. He writes again asking for the rest, and asks God not to send it by mail because the post office employees are "a bunch of crooks".
  • Themes: unshakeable faith; human kindness; irony — the very people who helped him are the ones Lencho accuses.
  • Characters: Lencho — hardworking, simple, deeply religious, naive and ungrateful without realising it. Postmaster — kind, generous, a man of action, wants to preserve faith.

Worked examples

Example 1 (3 marks): "What is ironic about the ending of the story?" → the postmaster and employees collected money to help Lencho (1); Lencho accuses them of stealing part of it (1); those who helped him are called crooks — situational irony (1).

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) How much money did the postmaster send Lencho? (a) 100 pesos (b) 70 pesos (c) 50 pesos (d) 30 pesos. Answer: (b).
  2. (3 marks) Why did the postmaster decide to answer Lencho's letter? Answer: he was moved by Lencho's firm faith in God (1); he did not want that faith to be shaken (1); so he collected money and replied, signing it "God" (1).
  3. (6 marks) "Lencho's faith was matched by the postmaster's kindness." Discuss the two characters and the irony of the story in about 100–120 words. Answer: Lencho's simple, total faith — writes to God (1.5); the postmaster's compassion — collects money, gives his own salary (1.5); the irony of Lencho calling the helpers crooks (1.5); message: faith and kindness, and the danger of misjudging others (1.5).

Common mistakes

  1. Saying the rain alone destroyed the crop (it was hail). 2. Wrong amount. 3. Calling Lencho greedy rather than naive. 4. Missing the irony. 5. Retelling the whole story instead of answering the question.

Quick recall

  1. What destroyed the crop? 2. How much did Lencho ask for? 3. What did the postmaster sign? 4. Who did Lencho accuse? 5. Main theme?

Answers: 1) A hailstorm. 2) 100 pesos. 3) "God". 4) Post office employees. 5) Faith, kindness and irony.
